claim: Retinal degeneration in mammals causes permanent loss of vision due to an inability to regenerate naturally.
source: Retinal degeneration in mammals causes permanent loss of vision, due to an inability to regenerate naturally.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about mammalian retinal degeneration.

claim: Some non-mammalian vertebrates show robust retinal regeneration via Muller glia.
source: Some non-mammalian vertebrates show robust regeneration, via Muller glia (MG).
evidence: This is established knowledge about regenerative capacity in non-mammalian vertebrates.

claim: Transgenic expression of Ascl1 in adult mouse Muller glia can stimulate regeneration of functional neurons.
source: We have recently made significant progress in stimulating adult mouse MG to regenerate functional neurons by transgenic expression of the proneural transcription factor Ascl1.
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' previous work and is referenced in the introduction.

claim: The efficacy of Ascl1-mediated neuronal regeneration from Muller glia is limited.
source: While these results showed that MG can serve as an endogenous source of neuronal replacement, the efficacy of this process is limited.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of previous work and provides motivation for the current study.

claim: A small molecule screen was designed using sci-Plex to identify compounds that promote neurogenesis.
source: With the goal of improving this in mammals, we designed a small molecule screen using sci-Plex, a method to multiplex up to thousands of single-nucleus RNA-seq conditions into a single experiment.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: The screen tested a library of 92 compounds.
source: We used this technology to screen a library of 92 compounds, identified, and validated two that promote neurogenesis in vivo.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the number of compounds screened.

claim: Two compounds from the screen were validated to promote neurogenesis in vivo.
source: We used this technology to screen a library of 92 compounds, identified, and validated two that promote neurogenesis in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: In mammalian species, retinal neurodegeneration results in permanent visual impairment because the CNS lacks endogenous regenerative capacity.
source: In mammalian species, retinal neurodegeneration results in permanent visual impairment because the central nervous system (CNS) lacks an endogenous regenerative capacity.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about mammalian CNS regeneration.

claim: Many non-mammalian vertebrates can replace lost neurons via neurogenic reprogramming of non-neuronal cells.
source: In contrast, many non-mammalian vertebrates can replace lost neurons via neurogenic reprogramming of non-neuronal cells (Todd and Reh, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Efforts to stimulate neural cell replacement in mammals have been met with some success.
source: Efforts to stimulate neural cell replacement in mammals, akin to what occurs in regenerative species, have been met with some success (Jorstad et al., 2017; Lentini et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Approaches to stimulate neural cell replacement typically focus on using transcription factors to reprogram glial cells into neurogenic precursors.
source: These approaches are typically focused on using transcription factors (TFs) to reprogram glial cells into neurogenic precursors in contexts across the CNS (brain, retina, and spinal cord).
evidence: This describes the general approach in the field based on established knowledge.

claim: Reprogramming of glial cells to neurons is incomplete, affecting only a subset of cells or producing cells without mature neuronal markers.
source: However, the reprogramming is incomplete, affecting only a subset of cells or producing cells without mature neuronal markers.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations of current approaches based on the literature.

claim: Viral overexpression of Ascl1 in primary Muller glia from young mice can reprogram glia to acquire a neurogenic progenitor state and generate neurons in vitro.
source: The in vitro viral overexpression of Ascl1 in primary MG is able to reprogram glia from young mice to acquire a neurogenic progenitor state and generate neurons (Pollak et al., 2013; Gascón et al., 2016), and similar results have been obtained with brain astrocytes (Pollak et al., 2013; Gascón et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Similar neurogenic reprogramming results have been obtained with brain astrocytes.
source: The in vitro viral overexpression of Ascl1 in primary MG is able to reprogram glia from young mice to acquire a neurogenic progenitor state and generate neurons (Pollak et al., 2013; Gascón et al., 2016), and similar results have been obtained with brain astrocytes (Pollak et al., 2013; Gascón et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ascl1 can stimulate a neurogenic state in Muller glia in vivo using a transgenic mouse line that targets Ascl1 specifically to Muller glia.
source: Ascl1 can also stimulate a neurogenic state in MG in vivo using a transgenic mouse line that targets this TF specifically to MG.
evidence: This describes the in vivo experimental approach used in previous studies.

claim: When transgenic mice expressing Ascl1 in Muller glia are subjected to NMDA injury and treated with HDAC inhibitors, the Muller glia regenerate functional neurons in adult mice.
source: When these mice are subjected to retinal injury using a neurotoxic dose of NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) and subsequently treated with histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitors, the MG regenerate functional neurons in adult mice (Jorstad et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Combining Ascl1 with other transcription factors has proven useful in stimulating glia to regenerate alternate arrays of neuronal fates.
source: Follow-up studies combining Ascl1 with other TFs have proven useful in stimulating glia to regenerate alternate arrays of neuronal fates (Todd et al., 2021; Todd et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The efficacy of neurogenesis from reprogrammed glia is often too low to provide enough cells for functional recovery.
source: These findings have established glia as a promising source for new neurons that could potentially be used to treat neurodegenerative disorders; however, the efficacy of neurogenesis is often too low to provide enough cells for functional recovery.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations based on previous work.

claim: Cell signaling molecules can affect the process of reprogramming cell fates.
source: Several studies have shown that cell signaling molecules can also affect the process of reprogramming cell fates, and investigators have suggested that small molecules might be useful in optimizing this approach for clinical applications of neural repair in combination or separate from TF overexpression (Jorstad et al., 2020; Gascón et al., 2016; Janowska et al., 2019; Cheng et al., 2015; Gao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Small molecules might be useful in optimizing neural repair approaches for clinical applications.
source: Several studies have shown that cell signaling molecules can also affect the process of reprogramming cell fates, and investigators have suggested that small molecules might be useful in optimizing this approach for clinical applications of neural repair in combination or separate from TF overexpression (Jorstad et al., 2020; Gascón et al., 2016; Janowska et al., 2019; Cheng et al., 2015; Gao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on previous studies.

claim: Traditional single-cell sequencing methods are too costly for most labs to perform for more than a handful of samples.
source: While traditional single-cell sequencing methods enable the molecular characterization of all cell types in a culture using low cell input without the need for marker genes, they are too costly for most labs to perform for more than a handful of samples.
evidence: This is a statement about practical limitations of traditional methods based on general knowledge.

claim: sci-Plex scales the number of samples within a single-cell sequencing experiment to up to thousands of samples.
source: sci-Plex, a combinatorial indexing-based technology, scales the number of samples within a given single-cell sequencing experiment to up to thousands of samples, overcoming such limitations (Srivatsan et al., 2020; Srivatsan et al., 2020; Cao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous publications describing sci-Plex.

claim: Current applications of sci-Plex have been performed in combination with sci-RNA-seq3 using culturing systems or organisms where cell number is not limited.
source: However, current applications of sci-Plex have been performed in combination with the high-throughput sci-RNA-seq3 protocol using culturing systems or organisms in which cell number is not limited (Srivatsan et al., 2020; Saunders et al., 2022; Dorrity et al., 2022; Tresenrider et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous applications of sci-Plex.

claim: sci-Plex is compatible with lower input samples in combination with the sci-RNA-seq2 protocol.
source: Here, we demonstrate that sci-Plex is also compatible with lower input samples in combination with the sci-RNA-seq2 protocol which requires a lower cell input and has a higher cell recovery rate.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study demonstrated through experimental data.

claim: This application of sci-Plex to reprogramming Muller glia is the first demonstration of sci-Plex's utility for screening chemical compounds in a low abundance primary cell type with disease relevance.
source: Our application of sci-Plex to reprogramming MG is the first demonstration of sci-Plex's utility for screening chemical compounds in a low abundance primary cell type with disease relevance.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the approach based on the authors' knowledge of the field.

claim: Increasing the length of Ascl1 exposure increased the number of neurons produced.
source: We saw that, increasing the length of Ascl1 exposure increased the number of neurons produced, and we uncovered molecular features associated with progression toward the neuronal fate.
evidence: This is a finding from the timecourse experiment supported by experimental data.

claim: Molecular features associated with progression toward the neuronal fate were uncovered.
source: We saw that, increasing the length of Ascl1 exposure increased the number of neurons produced, and we uncovered molecular features associated with progression toward the neuronal fate.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by gene expression analysis.

claim: The small molecule screen uncovered compounds that had effects on neurogenesis and total cell recovery.
source: When we applied sci-Plex to a small molecule screen for factors associated with stem cell biology, we uncovered compounds that had effects on neurogenesis and total cell recovery.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the screen supported by experimental data.

claim: Two compounds significantly enhanced neurogenesis in adult mouse retina in vivo.
source: The results of this secondary in vivo screen identified two compounds that significantly enhanced neurogenesis in adult mouse retina.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the in vivo validation experiments supported by experimental data.

claim: Retinas were isolated from P11 mice expressing a constitutive rtTA driving a tet-inducible Ascl1-GFP.
source: Retinas were isolated from P11 mice expressing a constitutive rtTA driving a tet-inducible Ascl1-GFP.
evidence: This describes the experimental materials and methods used.

claim: The retinas were dissociated and grown to enrich for Muller glia.
source: The retinas were dissociated and grown as previously described to enrich for MG (Pollak et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used, supported by a citation.

claim: Induction of Ascl1 by addition of doxycycline induces neurogenesis in Muller glia.
source: We have previously shown that induction of Ascl1, by addition of doxycycline to the medium, induces neurogenesis in the MG, and that the new neurons generated from the reprogrammed MG most closely resemble bipolar neurons (Pollak et al., 2013; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by previous work (citation) and referenced in Figure 1A.

claim: New neurons generated from reprogrammed Muller glia most closely resemble bipolar neurons.
source: We have previously shown that induction of Ascl1, by addition of doxycycline to the medium, induces neurogenesis in the MG, and that the new neurons generated from the reprogrammed MG most closely resemble bipolar neurons (Pollak et al., 2013; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by previous work (citation) and referenced in Figure 1A.

claim: Ascl1 was induced in replicate for 1-5 days at varying windows of time to temporally track the conversion of MG to neurons.
source: Taking advantage of the ease by which condition number can be scaled with sci-Plex, we induced Ascl1 in replicate for 1–5 days at varying windows of time, allowing us to temporally track the conversion of MG to neurons (Figure 1A, B).
evidence: This describes the experimental design shown in Figures 1A and 1B.

claim: 12,850 cells were recovered across two experiments and 30 wells.
source: We recovered 12,850 cells across two experiments and 30 wells (Timecourse: 7004, Pulse: 5846) with a median UMI (unique molecular identifier) count of 3172 and 2398 after all filtering steps, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–K).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiments shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The median UMI count was 3172 for the Timecourse experiment and 2398 for the Pulse experiment.
source: We recovered 12,850 cells across two experiments and 30 wells (Timecourse: 7004, Pulse: 5846) with a median UMI (unique molecular identifier) count of 3172 and 2398 after all filtering steps, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–K).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiments.

claim: The hash recovery rate was 68% for both experiments.
source: The hash recovery rate was 68% for both experiments (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D, G, H).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiments shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Most cells fell into one of four clusters: MG, Progenitor-like cells (ProL), Transition, and neuronal precursors (NeuPre).
source: Most cells fell into one of four clusters: (1) MG; (2) Progenitor-like cells (ProL); (3) Transition; and (4) neuronal precursors (NeuPre).
evidence: This describes the cell type annotation results from clustering analysis.

claim: Other clusters of non-MG-derived cells were identified, including microglia, astrocytes, and fibroblast-like cells.
source: In addition, we identified other clusters of non-MG-derived cells, including microglia, astrocytes, and fibroblast-like cells (FibroL), potentially derived from vascular cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This describes additional cell types identified in the analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Fibroblast-like cells are potentially derived from vascular cells.
source: In addition, we identified other clusters of non-MG-derived cells, including microglia, astrocytes, and fibroblast-like cells (FibroL), potentially derived from vascular cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an inference about the origin of fibroblast-like cells.

claim: When Ascl1 was maintained for the entire 5 day period, the distribution of cells across pseudotime was similar to that observed in the Timecourse experiment.
source: When Ascl1 was maintained for the entire 5 day period (Figure 1D, E), the distribution of cells across pseudotime was similar to that observed in the Timecourse experiment, with few MG remaining.
evidence: This is a comparison of results between experimental conditions shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: When Ascl1 was expressed for 2 or fewer days, almost all cells were identified as MG.
source: When Ascl1 was expressed in the cells for 2 or fewer days, almost all of the cells were identified as MG (Figure 1E, F).
evidence: This is a result from the Pulse experiment shown in Figures 1E and F.

claim: After 3 or more days of Ascl1 expression, transition and neurogenic precursor cells began to accumulate.
source: After 3 or more days of Ascl1 expression, transition and neurogenic precursor (NeuPre) cells began to accumulate, though a substantial number of MG were also present even after 4 days of Ascl1 exposure and 1 day without when compared to the Timecourse experiment (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is a result from the Pulse experiment shown in figures.

claim: After 4 days of Ascl1 expression, removal of Ascl1 allows a subset of cells to return to a glial state, while another subset remains committed to their neuronal fate.
source: These results suggest that even after 4 days of Ascl1 expression, removal of Ascl1 allows a subset of the cells to return to a glial state, while another subset of cells that have made it far enough along the reprogramming trajectory are no longer dependent on Ascl1 to remain committed to their neuronal fate.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results from the Pulse experiment.

claim: The local minima of pseudotime density plots from the Pulse experiment was found to be 16.
source: We found the local minima (10 < pseudotime < 20) of pseudotime density plots from the Pulse experiment to be 16 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from analysis shown in supplementary figure.

claim: The accumulation of cells with a pseudotime value >16 encompasses the population of cells that remain in the NeuPre or Bipolar fate even after removal of Ascl1 induction.
source: The accumulation of cells with a pseudotime value of >16 encompasses the population of cells that remain in the NeuPre or Bipolar fate even after removal of Ascl1 induction.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pseudotime analysis results.

claim: In the Timecourse experiment, decreased Ascl1 expression is observed at pseudotime values >16.
source: Coincidentally, in the Timecourse experiment, decreased Ascl1 expression is observed at pseudotime values >16 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a result from gene expression analysis shown in supplementary figure.

claim: Decreased Ascl1 expression with continued exposure to the induction signal is a phenomenon consistently observed in both in vitro and in vivo reprogramming paradigms.
source: While seemingly surprising, this decrease in Ascl1 expression with continued exposure to the induction signal is a phenomenon we consistently observe in both our in vitro and in vivo reprogramming paradigms (Todd et al., 2021; Todd and Reh, 2022; Todd et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: It is possible that mature neurons have a mechanism to downregulate Ascl1.
source: We do not have definitive knowledge of the mechanism behind how Ascl1 expression is repressed, but it is possible that mature neurons have a mechanism to downregulate it.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about a possible mechanism.

claim: Three major regulatory patterns were observed in the top 250 most differentially expressed genes: increasing, transient increase, and decreasing.
source: In the top 250 most differentially expressed genes, three major regulatory patterns (Cluster 1: increasing, Cluster 2: a transient increase, Cluster 3: decreasing) were observed (Figure 1G, H).
evidence: This is a result from differential gene expression analysis shown in Figures 1G and H.

claim: The downregulation of Id1 and Id3 in Cluster 2 was consistent with known biology.
source: The downregulation of Id1 and Id3 in Cluster 2 was consistent with known biology: these factors (1) form heterodimers with bHLH TFs making them incapable of binding their target sites (Roschger and Cabrele, 2017) and (2) have been previously implicated in maintaining retinal progenitors and MG in a progenitor state (Jorstad et al., 2017; Pollak et al., 2013; Jorstad et al., 2020; Todd et al., 2021; Todd et al., 2022; Ueki et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and known molecular mechanisms.

claim: Id factors form heterodimers with bHLH TFs making them incapable of binding their target sites.
source: The downregulation of Id1 and Id3 in Cluster 2 was consistent with known biology: these factors (1) form heterodimers with bHLH TFs making them incapable of binding their target sites (Roschger and Cabrele, 2017) and (2) have been previously implicated in maintaining retinal progenitors and MG in a progenitor state (Jorstad et al., 2017; Pollak et al., 2013; Jorstad et al., 2020; Todd et al., 2021; Todd et al., 2022; Ueki et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Id factors have been previously implicated in maintaining retinal progenitors and MG in a progenitor state.
source: The downregulation of Id1 and Id3 in Cluster 2 was consistent with known biology: these factors (1) form heterodimers with bHLH TFs making them incapable of binding their target sites (Roschger and Cabrele, 2017) and (2) have been previously implicated in maintaining retinal progenitors and MG in a progenitor state (Jorstad et al., 2017; Pollak et al., 2013; Jorstad et al., 2020; Todd et al., 2021; Todd et al., 2022; Ueki et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Genes in Cluster 1 that increase during the progenitor-to-neuron transition are associated with normal development of neurons.
source: Genes in Cluster 1, which increase during the progenitor-to-neuron transition, are also associated with the normal development of neurons (Elavl3, Map2) and with processes such as neuronal maturation and synaptogenesis (Nrxn3, Syt1).
evidence: This is an interpretation of gene expression patterns based on known gene functions.

claim: Four transcription factors increased in expression right around the loss of Ascl1 dependence: Sox4, Neurog2, Myt1, and Rorb.
source: There were also four TFs that increased in their expression right around the loss of Ascl1 dependence: Sox4, Neurog2, Myt1, and Rorb.
evidence: This is a result from the differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Sox4, Neurog2, Myt1, and Rorb are all expressed in the retina during the early stages of neurogenesis.
source: All of these genes are expressed in the retina during the early stages of neurogenesis (Vasconcelos et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2019; Hufnagel et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2017; Usui et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Myt1 is a direct target of Ascl1.
source: Of note, Myt1 is a direct target of Ascl1 and although it has been studied more thoroughly in the brain, it is associated with repression of progenitor gene expression programs (Vasconcelos et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Myt1 is associated with repression of progenitor gene expression programs.
source: Of note, Myt1 is a direct target of Ascl1 and although it has been studied more thoroughly in the brain, it is associated with repression of progenitor gene expression programs (Vasconcelos et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Rorb is involved in the specification of photoreceptor, amacrine, and horizontal but not bipolar cell fates.
source: Another factor on the list, Rorb is involved in the specification of photoreceptor, amacrine, and horizontal but not bipolar cell fates (Liu et al., 2013; Swaroop et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The screen tested compounds from the TocriScreen Stem Cell Library.
source: We screimed to assess the ability of sci-Plex to assign cells to specific wells in an expected manner by observing the in vfrom the TocriScreen Stem Cell Library (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This describes the source of compounds used in the screen.

claim: The compounds target a range of biological functions with a bias toward epigenetic modulators and modulators of common signaling pathways.
source: The compounds target a range of biological functions with a bias toward epigenetic modulators and modulators of common signaling pathways (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the characteristics of the compound library shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Small molecules were added at the same time as doxycycline and remained in culture until cells were collected on Day 5.
source: Small molecules from the TocrisScreen Stem Cell Library were added at the same time as the doxycycline and remained in culture until the cells were collected on Day 5 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The compounds were applied across three doses (0.1, 1, and 10 uM).
source: The compounds were applied across three doses (0.1, 1, and 10 uM) with each compound being tested on one of two different collection days.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: Three wells per collection day included only doxycycline (Only Ascl1) and three wells per collection day had no doxycycline (No Ascl1).
source: We included three wells per collection day in which only doxycycline was added (Only Ascl1) and three wells per collection day in which doxycycline was not added (No Ascl1).
evidence: This describes the control conditions in the experimental design.

claim: 92 small molecules and two control conditions were screened from a total of 265 individual wells after filtering.
source: In sum, we screened 92 small molecules and two control conditions from a total of 265 individual wells after filtering out conditions with low cell recovery.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental scale.

claim: 27,152 cells were profiled using sci-RNA-seq2.
source: We used sci-RNA-seq2 to profile a total of 27,152 cells (Collection 1: 6282, Collection 2: 20,870) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–G).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the screen.

claim: The median UMI count was 3551 for Collection 1 and 2166 for Collection 2.
source: The median UMI count was 3551 for Collection 1 and 2166 for Collection 2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H, I).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the screen shown in supplementary figures.

claim: A hash could be called for 65-74% of the cells.
source: A hash could be called for 65–74% of the cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result about hash assignment efficiency.

claim: The molecules that most markedly increased the percentage of Neurons included DBZ, DMH-1, RepSox, SB 431542, and WH-4-023.
source: The molecules that most markedly increased the percentage of Neurons, included DBZ (Milano et al., 2004), DMH-1 (Hao et al., 2010), RepSox (Ichida et al., 2009; Gellibert et al., 2004), SB 431542 (Inman et al., 2002; Laping et al., 2002), and WH-4-023 (Theunissen et al., 2014; Clark et al., 2012; Martin et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the screen with citations for each compound.

claim: DBZ, DMH-1, RepSox, SB 431542, and WH-4-023 target one of three molecular signaling pathways: Notch, BMP/TGF-beta, and LCK/SRC.
source: These compounds target one of three molecular signaling pathways: Notch, BMP/TGF-beta, and LCK/SRC.
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular targets of the identified compounds based on known mechanisms.

claim: For metformin, sodium 4-phenylbutyrate, and valproic acid, far more total cells were recovered than average.
source: We also calculated the number of cells recovered per well, and noticed that for a few treatments, far more total cells, regardless of cell type identity, were recovered than average. This was most prominent for metformin, sodium 4-phenylbutyrate, and valproic acid (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a result from the screen shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Both sodium 4-phenylbutyrate and valproic acid are HDAC inhibitors.
source: Both sodium 4-phenylbutyrate and valproic acid are HDAC inhibitors which is of interest because TSA (Trichostatin A), another HDAC inhibitor, is a significant stimulus for Ascl1-dependent reprogramming in vivo (Jorstad et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular mechanism of these compounds, supported by a citation.

claim: TSA is a significant stimulus for Ascl1-dependent reprogramming in vivo.
source: Both sodium 4-phenylbutyrate and valproic acid are HDAC inhibitors which is of interest because TSA (Trichostatin A), another HDAC inhibitor, is a significant stimulus for Ascl1-dependent reprogramming in vivo (Jorstad et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Metformin is a compound approved for the treatment of diabetes with other potential clinical uses.
source: Unexpectedly, metformin, a compound that is approved for the treatment of diabetes with other potential clinical uses (Cicero et al., 2012), also increased cell recovery in our assay.
evidence: This is a statement about the clinical use of metformin supported by a citation.

claim: Metformin has not been evaluated in the context of retinal reprogramming.
source: Because metformin has not been evaluated in the context of retinal reprogramming, we decided to pursue it and the five compounds that increased neurogenesis with further experiments in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of testing metformin in this context.

claim: Six compounds were selected for follow-up investigations in vivo.
source: Thus, the use of sci-Plex aided us in narrowing down 92 compounds to 6 for follow-up investigations.
evidence: This is a summary of the screening results.

claim: Previously undetected cell states were detected in the screen.
source: In addition to detecting shifts along the reprogramming trajectory, we also detected what appeared to be previously undetected cell states (Figure 2C, Unknown clusters).
evidence: This is a finding from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Cluster Unknown 1 was enriched with genes related to ER stress.
source: Cluster Unknown 1 was enriched with genes related to ER stress, Unknown 2 had markers of Immune reactive cells, and Unknown 3 had non-retinal neuronal characteristics (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–C, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is a result from GO term enrichment analysis shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Unknown 2 had markers of immune reactive cells.
source: Cluster Unknown 1 was enriched with genes related to ER stress, Unknown 2 had markers of Immune reactive cells, and Unknown 3 had non-retinal neuronal characteristics (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–C, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is a result from GO term enrichment analysis shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Unknown 3 had non-retinal neuronal characteristics.
source: Cluster Unknown 1 was enriched with genes related to ER stress, Unknown 2 had markers of Immune reactive cells, and Unknown 3 had non-retinal neuronal characteristics (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–C, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is a result from GO term enrichment analysis shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Treatments that lead to increased cell counts in the ER stressed cluster include two bromodomain inhibitors (I-BET 151 dihydrochloride, CPI 203).
source: The treatments that lead to increased cell counts in the ER stressed cluster include two bromodomain (acetylated lysine binders) inhibitors (I-BET 151 dihydrochloride, CPI 203) (Devaiah et al., 2012; Dawson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a result from the cell type composition analysis with citations for the compounds.

claim: In vivo MG express the signaling pathways targeted by the small molecule compounds during neurogenic reprogramming.
source: Before testing compounds from the in vitro screen in vivo, we sought to validate that in vivo MG express the signaling pathways targeted by our small molecule compounds during neurogenic reprogramming.
evidence: This is a rationale for the in vivo validation experiments.

claim: scRNA-seq libraries were made from in vivo regeneration experiments using mice engineered to express Ascl1 specifically in MG.
source: We analyzed scRNA-seq libraries made from our in vivo regeneration experiments where we used mice engineered to express Ascl1 specifically in the MG (Figure 3A), then induced retinal injury with an intravitreal injection of NMDA, and a co-injection of TSA (Figure 3B).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Mice were sacrificed and GFP expressing cells were sorted and subjected to 10× scRNA-seq either 5, 9, or 21 days after injury.
source: The mice were sacrificed and GFP expressing cells were sorted and subjected to 10× scRNA-seq either 5, 9, or 21 days after injury the day 5 and 9 libraries were originally published in Todd et al., 2020; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods with a citation to previous work.

claim: With increasing time after injury, greater numbers of MG-derived bipolar cells are observed.
source: As expected, with increasing time after injury, we observe greater numbers of MG-derived bipolar cells. This is most evident in the time between 9 and 21 days.
evidence: This is a result from the in vivo time course analysis.

claim: There is a small increase in bipolar cells between 5 and 9 days.
source: However, even between 5 and 9 days there is a small increase in bipolar cells.
evidence: This is a result from the in vivo time course analysis.

claim: A shift in the MG cluster toward a more mature state became apparent by 9 days.
source: Additionally, when pseudotime analysis was performed, a shift in the MG cluster toward a more mature state became apparent even by 9 days (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This is a result from pseudotime analysis shown in figures.

claim: Key target genes for each of the drugs are expressed early and decrease over time during reprogramming.
source: Lastly, using the pseudotime analysis across all time points, we looked at how the expression of key target genes for each of the drugs are expressed throughout the reprogramming process (Figure 3F). In all cases, at least some of the target genes are expressed early and decrease over time, making them ideal candidates for small molecule intervention.
evidence: This is a result from gene expression analysis across pseudotime shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Five hits were validated in vivo: DBZ, WH-4-023, metformin, DMH-1, and SB43152.
source: Using the same mice as above, we aimed to validate five hits in vivo (the γ-secretase inhibitor DBZ, Lck and Src inhibitor WH-4-023, LKB1/AMPK activator metformin, the BMP inhibitor DMH-1, and the TGF-BR1 inhibitor SB43152) for their ability to increase neurogenic reprogramming of MG in vivo.
evidence: This describes the in vivo validation experiments.

claim: RepSox and SB43152 have the same target.
source: We originally also identified RepSox as a hit, but because RepSox and SB43152 have the same target, we decided to only pursue SB43152.
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular targets of these compounds.

claim: Two compounds significantly boosted the number of Otx2+ neuronal cells: DBZ and metformin.
source: Out of the compounds tested, two significantly boosted the number of Otx2+ neuronal cells (Figure 3H–J, Figure 3—figure supplement 4A). The first identified compound was DBZ, a γ-secretase/Notch inhibitor (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the in vivo validation experiments shown in figures.

claim: DBZ is a γ-secretase/Notch inhibitor.
source: The first identified compound was DBZ, a γ-secretase/Notch inhibitor (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular mechanism of DBZ.

claim: The effect of DBZ is consistent with reports in the chick retina where γ-secretase inhibitor DAPT increased neuronal differentiation from proliferating MG.
source: This is consistent with reports in the chick retina where the γ-secretase inhibitor DAPT increased neuronal differentiation from proliferating MG (Hayes et al., 2007; Ghai et al., 2010; Todd et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies in chick retina.

claim: Inhibition of Notch is well known to promote neural differentiation from retinal progenitors in mouse and human.
source: Inhibition of Notch is also well known to promote neural differentiation from retinal progenitors in mouse and human (Finkbeiner et al., 2022; Nelson et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: DBZ represents a new compound found to promote neurogenesis in the mammalian retina.
source: While this result was not unexpected, DBZ represents a new compound found to promote neurogenesis in the mammalian retina.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding.

claim: Metformin showed the biggest effect on MG-neurogenesis.
source: The second positive hit, metformin, showed the biggest effect on MG-neurogenesis (Figure 3H, I).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the in vivo validation shown in figures.

claim: In some retinas, metformin increased the rate of neurogenesis to 75% of the Ascl1-expressing MG.
source: In some retinas, metformin increased the rate of neurogenesis to 75% of the Ascl1-expressing MG, a higher rate than any of our previous pharmaceutical treatments.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the in vivo validation experiments.

claim: The MG-derived neurons expressed Otx2 and were primarily located in the INL.
source: The MG-derived neurons expressed Otx2 and were primarily located in the INL (inner nuclear layer); this is similar to what we observe in the ANT treatment condition, and so it does not appear that metformin altered the fates of the MG-derived neurons;
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining analysis.

claim: Metformin does not appear to alter the fates of MG-derived neurons.
source: The MG-derived neurons expressed Otx2 and were primarily located in the INL (inner nuclear layer); this is similar to what we observe in the ANT treatment condition, and so it does not appear that metformin altered the fates of the MG-derived neurons;
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison to control conditions.

claim: The neurons in metformin treated retinas do not express markers of ganglion/amacrine cells.
source: In addition, the neurons in the metformin treated retinas do not express markers of ganglion/amacrine cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a result from immunostaining analysis shown in supplementary figure.

claim: The in vivo experiments confirm that in vitro sci-Plex screening is an effective method to identify new compounds that increase regeneration potential of mammalian MG.
source: These in vivo experiments thus confirm that the in vitro sci-Plex screening is an effective method to identify new compounds that increase the regeneration potential of mammalian MG.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the validation experiments.

claim: Most high-throughput screening assays use relatively limited read-outs such as cell morphology, proliferation or changes in expression of a reporter.
source: Most high-throughput screening assays use relatively limited read-outs, such as cell morphology, proliferation or changes in expression of a reporter.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations of conventional screening methods based on general knowledge.

claim: Many assays cannot access molecular information about responding cells or identify factors that make a cell type resistant to a treatment.
source: Many assays cannot access molecular information about responding cells or identify factors that make a cell type resistant to a treatment.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations of conventional screening methods.

claim: Single-cell transcriptomic assays overcome the hurdles of limited read-outs in conventional screening.
source: Single-cell transcriptomic assays overcome these hurdles, but the conventional protocols are costly and highly limited in sample number.
evidence: This is a statement about advantages and limitations of single-cell methods.

claim: This is the first demonstration of sci-Plex utility for studying reprogramming primary cells through screening drugs in low-input cultures and validating them in vivo.
source: Here, we demonstrate for the first time the utility of sci-Plex, an ultra-scalable scRNA-seq protocol, for studying reprogramming primary cells through screening drugs in low-input cultures and subsequently validating them in vivo.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the approach.

claim: The experiments identified drugs that support reprogramming and revealed underlying biology important for the progression of glial cell reprogramming.
source: Our experiments both identified drugs that support reprogramming and revealed underlying biology important for the progression of glial cell reprogramming.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's contributions.

claim: sci-Plex was used to pinpoint the moment during in vitro reprogramming at which cells become committed toward a neurogenic cell fate independent of continued Ascl1 expression.
source: We first used sci-Plex to pinpoint the moment during in vitro reprogramming at which cells become committed toward a neurogenic cell fate independent of continued Ascl1 expression.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the Pulse experiment.

claim: Myt1 was identified as a potentially critical factor for commitment toward the neuronal fate.
source: With our observation that cells no longer require Ascl1 to maintain their neuronal identity after a certain point along their reprogramming trajectory, we looked at the transcriptional regulators that were changing in their expression around this point and identified Myt1 as a potentially critical factor for commitment toward the neuronal fate.
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression analysis.

claim: Myt1 is a zinc finger-containing DNA-binding TF that is found specifically in neuronal cells and is important in neuronal differentiation.
source: Myt1 is a zinc finger-containing DNA-binding TF that is found specifically in neuronal cells and is important in neuronal differentiation (Vasconcelos et al., 2016; Bellefroid et al., 1996; Kim and Hudson, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In neural stem cells, the Myt1 promoter is bound by Ascl1 and protein expression is induced following overexpression of Ascl1.
source: In neural stem cells, the Myt1 promoter is bound by Ascl1 and protein expression is induced following the overexpression of Ascl1 (Vasconcelos et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Myt1 and Myt1l function by binding to and repressing their target genes which include non-neuronal genes, progenitor genes, and regulators of Notch signaling.
source: Myt1 and its family member Myt1l function by binding to and repressing their target genes which include non-neuronal genes, progenitor genes, and regulators of Notch signaling (Vasconcelos et al., 2016; Mall et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Myt1l has been associated with aiding in the in vitro reprogramming of fibroblasts to neurons.
source: Myt1l has also been associated with aiding in the in vitro reprogramming of fibroblasts to neurons (Vasconcelos et al., 2016; Mall et al., 2017; Vierbuchen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Little is known about Myt1's role in the retina.
source: However, little is known about its role in the retina, and no previous reports indicate a direct role for Myt1 in committing cells to the neuronal fate after the removal of other proneural TFs.
evidence: This is a statement about gaps in current knowledge.

claim: No previous reports indicate a direct role for Myt1 in committing cells to the neuronal fate after removal of other proneural TFs.
source: However, little is known about its role in the retina, and no previous reports indicate a direct role for Myt1 in committing cells to the neuronal fate after the removal of other proneural TFs.
evidence: This is a statement about gaps in current knowledge.

claim: DBZ targets the ability of gamma-secretase to cleave the intracellular domain of activated Notch receptors.
source: It targets the ability of gamma-secretase to cleave the intracellular domain of activated Notch receptors.
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular mechanism of DBZ.

claim: DBZ has not previously been used in retinal reprogramming studies.
source: While DBZ has not previously been used in retinal reprogramming studies, Notch is well known to affect neurogenesis and neural regeneration in the retina.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of using DBZ in this context.

claim: Notch is well known to affect neurogenesis and neural regeneration in the retina.
source: While DBZ has not previously been used in retinal reprogramming studies, Notch is well known to affect neurogenesis and neural regeneration in the retina.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Notch signaling in the retina.

claim: Pharmacological manipulation of Notch signaling has been used to alter the proliferative and neurogenic capacity of MG in fish and chick retina.
source: Pharmacological manipulation of Notch signaling has been used to alter the proliferative and neurogenic capacity of MG in fish and chick retina (Hayes et al., 2007; Ghai et al., 2010; Conner et al., 2014; Wan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Myt1 inhibits Notch signaling.
source: It is also interesting that Myt1, identified in our Pulse experiment as a factor that may prevent neuronal cells from returning to the progenitor fate, inhibits Notch signaling (Vasconcelos et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The screen recovering a γ-secretase inhibitor confirmed the ability of the workflow to identify important regulators.
source: That our screen recovered a γ-secretase inhibitor, in line with the known role of Notch in the retina, confirmed the ability of our workflow to identify important regulators.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the validation of the screening approach.

claim: Metformin is typically thought to work via AMPK.
source: Mechanistically, metformin is typically thought to work via AMPK, and while used clinically for Type2 diabetes, many studies have noted its neuroprotective and anti-neuroinflammatory effects (Markowicz-Piasecka et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous review.

claim: Many studies have noted metformin's neuroprotective and anti-neuroinflammatory effects.
source: Mechanistically, metformin is typically thought to work via AMPK, and while used clinically for Type2 diabetes, many studies have noted its neuroprotective and anti-neuroinflammatory effects (Markowicz-Piasecka et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous review.

claim: In the screen, metformin increased the total number of cells recovered, including those in the neurogenic precursor stage.
source: In our screen, metformin increased the total number of cells recovered by sci-Plex, including those in the neurogenic precursor stage.
evidence: This is a result from the screen.

claim: The effect of metformin on neurogenesis is consistent with promotion of neurogenesis reported in another in vitro study using mouse cortical and hippocampal progenitors and human ESC-derived neural progenitors.
source: The effect we find on neurogenesis is consistent with the promotion of neurogenesis reported in another in vitro study using mouse cortical and hippocampal progenitors and human ESC-derived neural progenitors (Wang et al., 2012), and may in part be mediated by Gadd45g, via DNA methylation (Zhang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Metformin's effect on neurogenesis may in part be mediated by Gadd45g via DNA methylation.
source: The effect we find on neurogenesis is consistent with the promotion of neurogenesis reported in another in vitro study using mouse cortical and hippocampal progenitors and human ESC-derived neural progenitors (Wang et al., 2012), and may in part be mediated by Gadd45g, via DNA methylation (Zhang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation.

claim: Metformin restored blood flow and vascular density in aged mice and promoted neurogenesis from the SVZ in vivo and in vitro.
source: Moreover, metformin restored blood flow and vascular density in aged mice and promoted neurogenesis from the SVZ in vivo and in vitro (Zhu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Reprogramming glia to serve as a source of neural repair is a strategy utilized by non-mammalian vertebrates.
source: Reprogramming glia to serve as a source of neural repair is a strategy utilized by non-mammalian vertebrates, and inspired by nature, we and others have shown that harnessing this latent neural regenerative capacity by proneural TF over-expression can revive the neuronal reprogramming program in mammals.
evidence: This is established knowledge about regenerative strategies.

claim: Harnessing latent neural regenerative capacity by proneural TF over-expression can revive the neuronal reprogramming program in mammals.
source: Reprogramming glia to serve as a source of neural repair is a strategy utilized by non-mammalian vertebrates, and inspired by nature, we and others have shown that harnessing this latent neural regenerative capacity by proneural TF over-expression can revive the neuronal reprogramming program in mammals.
evidence: This is supported by the authors' work and others in the field.

claim: Layering in the use of small molecules can increase the efficiency of reprogramming.
source: Layering in the use of small molecules can increase the efficiency of such reprogramming, and we show here that screening through larger libraries of compounds at single-cell resolution in vitro can point us toward new in vivo hits.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Screening through larger libraries of compounds at single-cell resolution in vitro can point toward new in vivo hits.
source: Layering in the use of small molecules can increase the efficiency of such reprogramming, and we show here that screening through larger libraries of compounds at single-cell resolution in vitro can point us toward new in vivo hits.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study demonstrating the utility of the approach.
